verdict: Booking's travel business kept growing — gross bookings rose 10% and room nights rose 7% — but a $900M FTC charge cut reported revenue by 1% and left net income almost flat at $2.7B.

kpis.label: Revenue growth
kpis.note: GAAP revenue was $8.9B; without the $900M FTC reduction, adjusted revenue rose 9% to $9.8B

kpis.label: EPS (GAAP diluted)
kpis.note: Up 7% from $3.38 a year ago — per-share figures reflect the 25-for-1 stock split on April 2, 2026

kpis.label: Gross bookings
kpis.note: Up 10% from a year ago; room nights rose 7% to 345 million

kpis.label: FTC revenue hit
kpis.note: A $900M revenue reduction plus a $100M accrued loss for an FTC matter involving Priceline — excluded from adjusted results

segments.name: Merchant revenues
segments.note: Booking collects the traveler's money itself and pays the hotel or airline — up 14% as Booking.com keeps shifting to this model

segments.name: Agency revenues
segments.note: Hotels and other providers pay Booking a commission and collect the traveler's money themselves — down 4% in the shift to merchant

segments.name: Advertising and other revenues
segments.note: Advertising on Booking's sites and OpenTable restaurant revenue — up 8%

segments.name: FTC matter
segments.note: A $900M reduction in revenue recorded for a possible FTC resolution involving Priceline — there was no such charge a year ago

opex.name: Marketing expenses
opex.note: Ads and partner marketing to bring in travelers — 4.8% of gross bookings, vs 4.7% a year ago

opex.name: Sales and other expenses
opex.note: Payment processing for merchant bookings and customer-service costs — merchant transaction costs rose $72M as merchant bookings grew

opex.name: Personnel
opex.note: Pay for about 25,850 employees, including $145M of stock-based pay — roughly flat from a year ago

opex.name: General and administrative
opex.note: Running the company — includes the $100M accrued loss for the FTC matter, which is why it rose 33%

opex.name: Information technology
opex.note: Cloud, software and generative AI costs — up 25%

opex.name: Depreciation and amortization
opex.note: Wear and tear on buildings, equipment and software — up 15%

opex.name: Transformation costs
opex.note: Costs of the company's transformation program — down from $105M a year ago; there was no impairment charge this quarter, vs $457M a year ago

takeaways.title: An FTC matter masked the growth
takeaways.text: Booking cut revenue by $900M and accrued another $100M in general and administrative costs for a possible FTC resolution involving Priceline's disclosures, fees, customer support and billing. Without it, adjusted revenue rose 9% to $9.8B and adjusted EPS rose 17% to $4.66.

takeaways.title: Merchant is now the engine
takeaways.text: Merchant revenue rose 14% to $7.0B as Booking collects more travelers' payments itself, while agency revenue fell 4% to $2.5B — the ongoing shift from agency to merchant at Booking.com.

takeaways.title: Travel demand stayed resilient
takeaways.text: Room nights rose 7% to 345 million and gross bookings rose 10% to $54.5B, even though softer long-haul international travel linked to the conflict in the Middle East weighed on demand late in the quarter.

oneTimers: FTC matter: a $900M reduction in revenue and a $100M accrued loss included in general and administrative expenses, after FTC staff said in July 2026 they intended to recommend a complaint against Priceline over disclosures, fees, customer support and billing. No settlement had been agreed, litigation remains possible, and the FTC could seek more than the amounts recorded.
Transformation costs were $23M in the quarter, down from $105M a year ago.
There was no impairment charge this quarter, compared with a $457M impairment a year ago.

Stock split: Booking completed a 25-for-1 stock split on April 2, 2026, and all share and per-share figures in the filings are retroactively adjusted — that is why GAAP EPS is $3.61, not a pre-split figure.
otherDetail: Net other income was just $5M: interest expense of -$311M, interest and dividend income of +$221M, and other income of +$95M. That $95M was $107M of foreign-currency transaction gains partly offset by $12M of other losses, including an $18M net loss on equity securities.
footerNote: Booking Holdings reports no cost of revenue — every cost is an operating expense, so gross profit equals revenue.
